record.issuing_body: Florida Senate (2026 Regular Session; sponsors Appropriations Committee and Sen. Leek)
record.summary: Would have created an 'Artificial Intelligence Bill of Rights'. Companion chatbot platforms would have needed parental consent for minors' accounts, given parents controls and self-harm alerts, reminded minors hourly that the chatbot is not human and guarded against material harmful to minors. Bot operators would have had to tell users hourly that they are not talking to a human, AI companies could sell or disclose users' personal information only as deidentified data, and commercial use of AI-generated likenesses would have needed consent. It would also have barred government AI contracts with entities tied to foreign countries of concern and regulated AI instructional tools in schools.
record.notes: Filed on 22 Dec 2025 and referred to Commerce and Tourism and to Appropriations. Commerce and Tourism reported it favourably (10-0) on 21 Jan 2026; Appropriations adopted a committee substitute (18-0) on 18 Feb 2026, which changed the definition of artificial intelligence, added further rights, a discretionary 45-day cure period and the rules on AI instructional tools. The Senate adopted two floor amendments and passed the bill 35-2 on 4 Mar 2026; it died in House messages on 13 Mar 2026. The bill stated an effective date of 1 Jul 2026. The Department of Legal Affairs would have enforced the chatbot, bot and data provisions as deceptive or unfair trade practices, with civil penalties of up to USD 50,000 per violation; a platform, operator or company facing an alleged violation could have shown the department controls aligned with the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and ISO 42001. Minors could have recovered up to USD 10,000 from a chatbot platform for knowing or reckless violations. The text the Senate passed barred schools from giving students AI instructional tools before grade 6, with exceptions, and required parental notice, an opt-out and parental account access. A bill with the same title and description, SB 2-D, was filed in Special Session D (US-FL-04); it passed the Senate 37-1 on 28 Apr 2026 and died in the House Information Technology Budget & Policy Subcommittee on 29 Apr 2026.

verification.note: Stored from flsenate.gov: the Senate bill page for CS/SB 482 (2026), the Commerce and Tourism analyses of 20 Jan 2026 (pre- and post-meeting), the Appropriations analysis of 20 Feb 2026, the first engrossed text (e1, posted 4 Mar 2026), and the bill page and Senate vote record of SB 2-D (2026D). The bill page confirms the title, the sponsors, the history from filing on 22 Dec 2025 to the 35-2 Senate vote on 4 Mar 2026 and 'Died in Messages' in the House on 13 Mar 2026, the posting of the engrossed text on 4 Mar 2026 and the 1 Jul 2026 effective date; the summary and notes rest on the engrossed text, which carries the floor amendments the Senate adopted when it passed the bill. The Florida Phoenix report of 4 Mar 2026 (secondary_url) could not be stored (HTTP 403 on 12 and 14 Oct 2026), so the Governor's backing of the bill and the House leadership's refusal to take it up, which the earlier version of the record stated, are not confirmed by any stored copy and are no longer stated; the sponsor's first name is also not in the stored copies.
